title: A probability distribution over the gait cycle: Probabilistic Movement Primitives on real knee kinematics

dataset.name: A public dataset of overground and treadmill walking kinematics and kinetics (WBDS)
dataset.record: 42 healthy adults, sagittal knee angle (RKneeAngleZ) at a comfortable treadmill speed (T04), time-normalised to the gait cycle (101 points)
dataset.citation: Fukuchi CA, Fukuchi RK, Duarte M. A public dataset of overground and treadmill walking kinematics and kinetics in healthy individuals. PeerJ 2018;6:e4640; data figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.5722711 (CC-BY 4.0).

proposition: A movement primitive stores not a single trajectory but a DISTRIBUTION over trajectories. On 42 subjects' real knee-angle gait cycles, a Probabilistic Movement Primitive recovers the population exactly: its mean matches the ensemble average (r = 1.000) and its +/-2 SD band is calibrated (95.0% of observed points fall inside). Gaussian via-point conditioning -- pinning the swing-flexion peak to a target -- pulls the mean 25.8 deg toward the target and collapses the uncertainty there (SD ratio ~0), adjusting the whole trajectory through the learned correlation.

claims.statement: correlation of the ProMP mean with the population ensemble mean
fraction of observed points inside the +/-2 SD band (Gaussian ~0.95)
uncertainty ratio at the via-point after conditioning (< 1 = shrinks)
how far the mean is pulled toward the via-point (deg)

validation.reference: A Probabilistic Movement Primitive is a Gaussian distribution over trajectories: (1) its mean trajectory must equal the population ensemble average; (2) its +/-2 SD band must be calibrated (about 95% coverage for Gaussian data); (3) Gaussian conditioning on a via-point must pull the mean through that point AND shrink the uncertainty there, propagating to the rest of the trajectory via the learned covariance -- the defining ProMP properties (Paraschos et al. 2013).
validation.data: REAL -- Fukuchi et al. 2018 (figshare 5722711), 42 subjects, sagittal knee gait kinematics
validation.note: All three defining ProMP properties reproduce on real data: the mean recovers the ensemble average (r = 1.000), the +/-2 SD band covers 95.0% of the observed knee-angle points (calibrated Gaussian), and pinning the swing-flexion peak (65% cycle) pulls the conditioned mean 25.8 deg toward the target while its SD at the via-point collapses to ~0 (obs_sd = 1e-3) and the adjustment spreads smoothly along the cycle. Honest scope: this models the BETWEEN-subject distribution of the ensemble-average cycle (a population 'gait template'); a within-subject stride-to-stride ProMP would need continuous multi-stride data. The band is a 2nd-order (Gaussian) summary; genuinely multi-modal gait populations would need a mixture.

open_questions.q: A within-subject stride-to-stride ProMP (rather than the between-subject ensemble distribution) needs continuous multi-stride joint-angle streams; and a mixture-of-ProMPs would capture multi-modal populations (e.g. mixed pathologies). Documented, not escalated.
